title: Neon Quota Rush
premise: A neon-soaked futuristic courier-scanner arcade game where the player spins three glowing reels to collect haul, meet rising shift quotas, and avoid failing the route before scans run out.
interaction_model: Single-screen pointer/tap arcade play centered on one main scan button, with optional shop interactions between spins to buy run upgrades.
objective: Reach each shift's money quota before exhausting the limited number of scans, using reel matches and upgrades to improve expected payouts.
progression: Each cleared shift increases the quota, resets current haul to zero, refreshes the scan count, and keeps purchased upgrades active for the ongoing run.
theme: Cyberpunk slot-inspired courier fantasy with scanner terminology, holographic HUD panels, glowing symbols, and synthwave presentation.
mood: Fast, flashy, arcade-like, tense, and reward-driven with celebratory jackpot feedback and sharp failure states.
likely_audience: players who enjoy quick arcade loops
players who like slot-style feedback without casino simulation depth
confidence_notes: High confidence in the core loop because the code explicitly defines three spinning reels, payout rules, level quotas, scans, and upgrades.
Moderate confidence in genre labeling because the fiction frames the game as a courier scanner, while the mechanics are most directly slot-machine-inspired arcade progression.
High confidence that touch/mobile play is intended due to pointer events, vibration hooks, safe-area spacing, and full-screen canvas layout.
recreation_prompt: Create a single-screen browser arcade game called "Neon Quota Rush" that feels like a cyberpunk slot-machine survival run re-themed as a futuristic courier scanner. The player taps one large SCAN button to spin three vertical neon reels on a full-screen canvas. Each reel shows glowing symbol icons like diamonds, sevens, bells, bars, cherries, and lemons, with different rarity weights and payout values. When the reels stop, matching all three center symbols should trigger a jackpot payout, and matching any two should trigger a smaller cache payout. Every scan consumes one limited attempt from a per-shift scan counter, and the player must earn enough money to fill a visible route quota bar before scans reach zero. If the quota is met, the game advances to the next shift, raises the quota substantially, refreshes the scan count, and keeps purchased upgrades active; if the player runs out of scans first, show a dramatic game-over panel with the final shift and total haul. Include a small upgrade shop called Rig Bay where the player can spend current haul on three permanent-for-the-run upgrades: better luck to improve rare symbol odds, a payout multiplier that increases all winnings, and extra scans added to future shifts. Present everything with a glossy neon HUD, glowing borders, sci-fi typography, jackpot text popups, particles, screen flashes, compact reaction GIFs, and energetic audio cues so the experience feels like a polished mobile-friendly synthwave arcade game rather than a realistic casino sim.
